newsitem.title: POLAND: RIGHTISTS ATTACK POLISH GOVERNMENT BANKING POLICY.
newsitem.headline: RIGHTISTS ATTACK POLISH GOVERNMENT BANKING POLICY.

text.p: The rightist Movement for Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) said on Friday that the current government led by ex-communists was trying to clinch its control of the banking sector before this year's elections.

"Before the coming parliamentary elections the current government set-up wants to take total control over the banking system, with the National Bank of Poland sitting idle," ROP leader Jan Olszewski told a news conference.
Poland is due to hold elections in September.
ROP, with a patriotic, populist programme and recent opinion poll ratings of between six and 11 percent, is an influential voice on the more radical right.
Olszewski said the central bank's recent sale of the Polish Investment Bank SA (PBI) to Kredyt Bank SA showed how the authorities wanted to gain influence in the sector.
He said good state-owned banks were being taken over by less strong, but politically well-connected private ones.
"The banking sector's ownership structure is systematically blurred and in this way private persons will be able to use public money without controls," Olszewski alleged.
He added that the moves would allow the currently ruling "nomenklatura" to retain influence over the financial system even if it lost the coming elections.

ROP said the new banking law drafted by the government, comprised of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Peasant party (PSL), would curb the influence of future governments and parliaments over state-owned banks.

ROP is aligned with the radical wing of the more powerful Solidarity Election Action (AWS), which is roughly neck and neck with the ex-communist SLD in recent polls. -- Pawel Florkiewicz +48 22 653 9700
